source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why should a preferred writing style be distinguished from a record of which file was published?

options.text: The writing style is a project fact that expires when a file is published.
options.feedback: A style preference can recur across tasks. Publishing a file changes project state without necessarily changing that preference.

options.text: The publication record is a preference for what should happen on the next task.
options.feedback: A publication record tracks what happened in this project. A recurring preference guides later choices rather than establishing completed operations.

options.text: Both records describe stable choices that can be reused without updating.
options.feedback: Preferences may recur, but a project record tracks changing facts. Reusing stale publication state can misrepresent what has actually been completed.

options.text: One can recur across tasks; the other tracks changing project facts.
options.feedback: A preference may guide many tasks, while project state records current decisions and operations. Maintaining both appropriately helps prevent stale assumptions.
